newsitem.title: USA: IMM currencies open mixed, yen rises on trade data.
newsitem.headline: IMM currencies open mixed, yen rises on trade data.

text.p: IMM currency futures opened mixed, with yen gaining after news overnight that Japan's trade surplus rose sharply in the first 20 days of June.
Japan's Finance Ministry said the 20-day surplus rose 129.3 percent on a year-over-year basis and suggested the total June figure would show a third consecutive monthly gain.
IMM currency traders said activity this morning was fairly quiet, with most of the action occurring overnight when the dollar fell to a low of 111.98 yen.
They attributed part of the movement in yen to activity in the yen/pound cross rate.
One currency analyst said technical factors were likely to overshadow the fundamentals in the foreign exchange market this week, barring any surprise comments by government officials.
Dollar/yen broke an important support level at 112.80 overnight and is poised to challenge 110.50 near term, the analyst said.
"I would expect dollar/yen to be on the defensive for the balance of the week," he said.
Japan will release May current account data Tuesday.
British pound futures were lower in a low-volume corrective setback from sterling's recent rapid ascent, traders and analysts said.

In addition, May manufacturing output in the country fell 1.1 percent in May, compared with expectations for a 0.2 percent rise, and industrial production was off 0.9 percent versus a forecast rise of 0.2 percent.
Overall, however, sterling's uptrend was seen as intact amid anticipation the Bank of England will raise interest rates at its Thursday policy meeting.
Mark futures gained slightly as dollar/mark retreated after failing to break above 1.7600 on the recent upmove.
Bavarian Premier Edmund Stoiber's comments in the Financial Times that a delay in European monetary union was preferable to a weak single currency boosted the mark early.
Furthermore, Bavarian Finance Minister Erwin Huber said EMU could start without France.
Australian dollar futures took a hit after the central bank's announcement Thursday that it sold 167 metric tonnes of gold this year.

September yen was up $0.000092 at $0.008988, marks were up $0.0022 at $0.5760, Swiss francs rose $0.0051 at $0.6922, sterling was down $0.0062 at $1.6810, Canadian dollars were up $0.0024 at $0.7320, Australian dollars were $0.0107 lower at $0.7435 and Mexican pesos rose $0.001100 at $0.123275. ((Chicago Derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
